Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/10/Text/10] Descriptive statistics (i.e. means and standard deviations) for women and men are shown in Table 1. Women, compared with men, had significantly higher scores in neuroticism and low self-esteem at all measurement occasions, significantly lower scores in avoidant attachment at all measurement occasions, and significantly higher scores in anxious attachment at T1. Women, compared with men, reported significantly higher relationship satisfaction at T2 and T3 and had significantly higher average levels of positive expectations and significantly higher variability of perceived responsiveness and self-disclosure. [/page/11/Text/5] Significant mean-level differences were found for women's neuroticism (between T1 and T3), for both couple members' low self-esteem (between T1 and T2 and between T1 and T3), and for both couple members' relationship satisfaction (between T1 and T2 and between T1 and T3).
